title: refuses a status that is not Accepted even when notarytool exits 0, and still asks for the log
why: The submission's status not read: notarytool exits 0 for a submission the notary rejected, so an Invalid image would be stapled and uploaded as notarised.

title: refuses a status that is not Accepted even when notarytool exits 0, and still asks for the log
why: The log asked for only after an acceptance: a rejected submission fails with no word of what the notary found, which the log alone says.

title: refuses an accepted submission whose log holds an error, and staples nothing
why: An error in the notary's log passed over as a warning: an accepted submission that still carries one would ship.

title: refuses an accepted submission whose log cannot be fetched, after three tries
why: A log that could not be read taken as a log with no issues: the run would call clean what it never saw.

find: const given = (env, name) => typeof env[name] === 'string' && env[name].trim() !== ''
title: submits nothing without credentials, naming what is empty
why: An empty secret taken as a value: the image is submitted with an empty issuer, and the failure is the notary's authentication error, which names nothing.

title: are refused in part, naming each empty variable, even beside a profile
why: A key given in part passed over for the keychain profile: a run with one secret missing would notarise as whoever the machine's profile is.

title: submits nothing with a key file that is missing, empty or not a key
why: An empty key file handed to notarytool: the secret that was never set surfaces as an authentication error that names no cause.

title: refuses when notarytool fails, times out or prints nothing it can read
why: notarytool's own failure not counted: a run that exited non-zero is judged only by whatever it managed to print.

title: refuses when the ticket cannot be stapled in three tries, or the staple does not validate
why: The stapler's exit status not read: an image with no ticket attached is uploaded as stapled, and opens only where Apple can be reached.

title: refuses when the ticket cannot be stapled in three tries, or the staple does not validate
why: The staple never validated: the run ends green on the stapler's word that it wrote something, not on a ticket that checks.

title: never prints a credential
why: The command shown as it is run: the key's path, its id and the issuer id are printed into a public job log.

title: adds up to a worst case that is a run at its slowest
why: The pauses left out of the worst case: a step limit set just past it can stop the script while it is still waiting for a try it would have made.

title: imports nothing but Node's own modules
why: An import that is not node: let through: the next one can be a package, on the runner that holds the notary's key and installs none.
